references.text: God blesses Noah and his sons with words similar to those given to Adam and Eve, urging them to be fruitful, multiply, and fill the earth.
God repeats the call to Noah and his descendants to be fruitful and multiply on the earth.
The psalm reflects on humanity's dominion over creation, including rule over animals, birds, and fish, in line with the mandate given in Genesis 1:28.
God also blesses the creatures of the sea and the birds, urging them to be fruitful and multiply, mirroring the blessing given to humans.
Reiterates that God created humanity in His image, blessed them, and called them human—a reference back to the creation mandate.
James refers to how humanity has tamed all kinds of animals, birds, reptiles, and sea creatures, reflecting the dominion mandate from creation.
The instruction to the animals to be fruitful after the flood, mirroring the creation mandate in 1:28 and highlighting God's care for all life.
The first part of the creation mandate that the waters should teem with life, which forms the foundation for the later call to humanity in 1:28.
The concretization of the creation mandate through Abraham's offspring, where the call to fruitfulness is linked to forming a people and kings.
God's promise to Jacob to make him fruitful and give him the land, as a specific application of the creation mandate from 1:28.
The affirmation of humanity's dominion over animals after the flood, which is a direct parallel to the creation mandate in 1:28.
The prophecy of God restoring Israel, where He promises to make people and animals numerous and fruitful, reflecting the creation mandate.
God's blessing of Israel with fruitfulness and abundance, as a specific application of the creation mandate in the promised land.
God's promise to Abraham to make his descendants numerous, as a specific application of the creation mandate from 1:28.
The call to Israel to listen to God's commands and become numerous, as a specific application of the creation mandate in the promised land.
God's promise to Abraham to make him exceedingly fruitful and into a nation, which is a specific application of the creation mandate from Genesis 1:28.
